## Summary
If the merchant dashboard allows arbitrary metadata to be passed into the vault initialization, it could lead to bloated storage or injection vectors. The contract should sanitize or strictly limit the length of metadata strings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add a maximum length constraint (e.g. 64 bytes) to merchant metadata fields.
- [ ] Revert the transaction if the input exceeds the limit.
- [ ] Write tests verifying the length restrictions are enforced.

## Summary
The TTL (Time To Live) extension logic is critical for preventing data loss, but the boundary conditions (e.g. extending exactly at the threshold, or extending past the maximum ledger limit) are not thoroughly tested.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Use property-based testing (like `proptest`) to fuzz the TTL extension logic.
- [ ] Verify behavior when the current ledger is exactly at the extension threshold.
- [ ] Verify the contract correctly handles maximum ledger boundaries without overflowing.

## Tech Stack
Rust, proptest

## Important

comments.body:
Assigning to @wagmiiii.

Unblocked as of PR #41 (2026-08-04) — this issue predates the TTL work it tests. The surface now exists to fuzz:

- `extend_batch_ttl(batch_id)` on `ReceiptAnchor` and `extend_refund_ttl(payment_ref)` on `RefundVault`, both public and unauthenticated by design.
- `TTL_EXTEND = 518_400` (~30 days at ~5s/ledger) and `TTL_THRESHOLD = 100`, the latter existing specifically so a bump is not written on every call — the threshold boundary is the interesting edge here.

Two cases worth including that are not obvious from the issue body: extending a record that is already archived, and repeated extension calls landing inside the threshold window, which should be no-ops rather than writes. Both are cheap to assert in the test environment and both are paths a caller can trigger from outside, since the extension functions take no auth.

title: test(contracts): fuzz test TTL extension boundaries and edge cases

## Summary
The contracts currently use `Persistent` storage for all data. Some data, like intermediate states or temporary nonces, could be moved to `Temporary` storage to significantly reduce rent fees on the Stellar network.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Audit all storage calls in the contracts.
- [ ] Migrate appropriate state from `Persistent` to `Temporary` storage.
- [ ] Document the reasoning for each change.
- [ ] Ensure all tests still pass and verify the storage types in the test environment.

## Tech Stack
Rust, soroban-sdk

## Important
Please make sure to read our [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/accensa/accensa-contracts/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before you start working on this issue.

comments.body:
Assigning to @wagmiiii with the rest of the contracts backlog.

The rent problem this issue targets has been partly addressed from the other direction since it was filed, so the scope should be trimmed before work starts.

Landed since:

- **TTL strategy** (PR #41, 2026-08-04) — `TTL_EXTEND`/`TTL_THRESHOLD` constants set to roughly 30 days of ledgers, with a threshold so a bump is not written on every call, plus public `extend_batch_ttl` and `extend_refund_ttl`.
- **Batch pruning** (PR #43, 2026-08-05) — `prune_batches(before_ledger)` reclaims rent on old anchored batches directly. Closed #22.

What remains is specifically the `Persistent` → `Temporary` audit in the acceptance criteria, and that audit is now smaller than it looks. `BatchRecord` and `RefundRecord` cannot move: both are the audit trail the product's verification claim rests on, and `Temporary` entries are unrecoverable once they expire rather than restorable like archived persistent ones. `DataKey::Admin`, `BatchCount`, `PrunedUpTo`, and the pause flag are instance storage and belong there.

So the honest version of this issue is: check whether anything is left that is genuinely reconstructible, and if nothing is, document that conclusion and close. That is still worth doing — "we audited it and persistent is correct" is a better answer than an open issue implying unclaimed savings — but it should not be scoped as a migration.

title: fix(contracts): optimize state storage to minimize rent fees

## Summary
The RefundVault manages merchant float and must be airtight against arithmetic overflows and unexpected inputs. We need fuzzy tests to bombard the deposit and refund logic with randomized, extreme inputs to ensure robust failure rather than undefined behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fuzz `deposit` with randomized extreme amounts (near i128::MAX).
- [ ] Fuzz concurrent or sequential `refund` and `withdraw` operations to check invariant preservation (e.g., balance cannot go negative).
- [ ] Add workflow step to run fuzz tests on PR.
